title: Zverev Reaches the Top of Men's Tennis
summary:
Alexander Zverev will replace Jannik Sinner as the men's world number one at his earliest opportunity after reaching the quarter-finals in Vienna. Already guaranteed to finish 2026 as the ATP's leading player, he made sure he will rise to the summit on Monday by beating Tallon Griekspoor 6-4 7-5 at the Erste Bank Open.

Zverev, 29, is the 30th man to become ATP world number one, and the second German to reach the pinnacle of the men's tour after Boris Becker in 1991. The achievement reflects his body of work this year, having won two Grand Slam titles and 64 of his 80 matches. He said it had been a wait, but sometimes you have to wait for the best things in life.

At the start of the year it seemed unthinkable that anybody other than Sinner or Carlos Alcaraz would become world number one. But injuries kept the dominant duo out for large chunks of the season, opening the door for Zverev's French Open and US Open titles.

Going into 2026, Alcaraz led the rankings with 12,050 points, closely followed by Sinner on 11,500, while third-ranked Zverev had 5,110 points. The pair had split all eight Grand Slam titles in 2024 and 2025 between them. He did not face a top-10 player until beating Ben Shelton in the New York final.

As the season entered its final stretch, Zverev secured the year-end number one ranking when Alcaraz lost in Shanghai on 12 October. Beating Griekspoor made him the first man other than Sinner and Alcaraz to top the rankings since Novak Djokovic in June 2024. Zverev conceded he would maybe not be the world's best player if both his rivals were healthy and at the top of their game, but he has efficiently beaten what has been in front of him, in the greatest season of his career. Next he faces British number one Arthur Fery in the quarter-finals.
why_it_matters: The top ranking is the sport's clearest measure of a season's best player, and Zverev's rise shows how injuries at the top can reshape a whole season — and how seizing that opening still takes a career-best year.

background_read: In men's tennis, the world number one ranking goes to the player with the best results over the season, and it can change hands when one player overtakes another.
The four Grand Slam tournaments are the biggest events in tennis, and winning them brings the most ranking points and prestige.
Injuries can keep even the best players out for long stretches, which can open the door for another player to climb to the top.
In such a season, the two players who began the year on top missed large parts of it, while another player kept winning.
